derivation: Two discrete axes: the products are 1, 2 for mode 1; 2, 4 for mode 2; 3, 6 for mode 3, so exactly two of the six cells fail - (mode 2, stage 2) and (mode 3, stage 2). Each axis owns its slice of its span (1 through 3 spans 2, 1 through 2 spans 1), which makes the cells disjoint and the union exactly the two failing branches. Neither axis carries the information alone: stage 2 is safe at mode 1, and mode 3 is safe at stage 1, so an instrument that treats a discrete axis as decoration cannot get this right by accident. Declared share 37.5%, within a factor of two of synthetic/quarter_2d, and the entry is also the one where an off-grid probe value would be most visible: a value between two modes is a branch of the table that does not exist.
